newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf Arabs call for end to Iran "occupation" of islands.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Arabs call for end to Iran "occupation" of islands.

text.p: Six Gulf Arab states called on Sunday for Iran to end what they said was its occupation of three Gulf islands also claimed by the United Arab Emirates.
The Gulf Cooperation Council's (GCC) Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and UAE said they were also concerned that Iran was building up its weapons arsenal.

A GCC statement issued after a two-day meeting of foreign ministers in Saudi Arabia said Iran was trying to maintain the "status quo by force" on the Abu Musa, Greater Tunb and Lesser Tunb islands, which lie near key oil shipping lanes.

"The council of ministers expressed its condemnation for the continuous Iranian steps on the UAE islands....it amounts to a violation of UAE sovereignty and aggression on its rights...and puts the whole region in danger," the GCC said.
It told Iran "to stop its occupation of the three islands".
Iran opened an airport on Abu Musa in March, and the GCC statement said it also built warehouses and factories.
The UAE said in April that Iran's building of a power plant on Greater Tunb violated UAE sovereignty.

The UAE has urged Iran to agree to take the row to the International Court of Justice. Iran says its sovereignty over the islands is not negotiable but it has called for bilateral talks with the UAE to clear up any "misunderstandings".
The GCC statement said the group was also "concerned about Iran's intention" to acquire conventional and non-conventional weapons "exceeding its legal defence needs".
Iran has said it has no desire to acquire nuclear weapons.
